title: Beau The Musical by Douglas Lyons and Ethan D. Pakchar at St. Luke’s ...
transcript: I was really excited to see Beau The Musical in its bigger and more customized venue, after catching its world premiere earlier this year. As far as I can tell, there aren't any major changes to the book or the score, which continues to be a highlight. The piece does generally feel stronger, though. It fills out a larger space quite nicely and I think this also affords them more clarity in the storytelling. It's a queer coming of age story, creatively framed as a dive bar set with Matt Rodin as the narrator and central character Ace Baker. Everyone doubles as a character and a musician, seamlessly transitioning between the different roles throughout the piece. And although the performers are constantly moving through the audience and all around the space, there's no lapse in emotional connection. Matt Rodin, as well as Jeb Brown who plays the titular character, are giving remarkably grounded performances. Their relationship is the heart of the whole piece, and it falls somewhat under the umbrella of mentorship from queer elders, which is something I feel like we don't see much of in our media, at least not in theatre. If these themes interest you, or if you're just in the market for a fresh and immersive musical, Beau should fit the bill. Beau was just extended into January at St. Luke's Theatre in Midtown. With that, another program for my collection.
